sources.title: GigaHubs Process Review Theory of Change
facts: The theory of change models benefits from connecting rural public buildings.
Expected benefits include public-service capability and potential surrounding network expansion.
The model is staged and geographic.
It is informed by prior evaluations and programme business cases.
Theory-of-change pathways must not be promoted as observed parcel outcomes.

sources.title: GigaHub Process Review Annex
facts: The annex documents data-modelling project scoping.
It also documents the case-study approach.
Evaluation design metadata is separate from programme-output data.
Case-study evidence cannot be generalised without the stated sampling limits.
Annex provenance should remain linked to the main process review.

sources.title: OMR and Public Review Subsidy Control Classification Guidance
facts: BDUK classifies premises as White, Grey, Black or Under Review.
Only White premises are eligible targets for subsidy under the stated guidance.
White means no qualifying gigabit infrastructure current or likely within three years.
Grey and Black classifications can include planned infrastructure.
Classification is an intervention decision input, not current service proof.

sources.title: Gigabit Broadband Voucher Scheme information
facts: GBVS supports premises outside suppliers' commercial plans and Project Gigabit contracts.
Eligible vouchers can contribute up to £4,500 toward installation costs.
Beneficiary validation occurs after a supplier reports completion.
BDUK may audit installations, speeds and installation quality.
Voucher eligibility or issue is not proof that a service is already live.

sources.title: Project Gigabit Evaluation Plan
facts: The evaluation covers GIS and GBVS interventions.
GIS subsidises network delivery where commercial rollout is not expected.
GBVS supports community-led extensions through vouchers.
GigaHubs is evaluated under a separate Hubs evaluation plan.
Evaluation outcomes must be separated from operational coverage evidence.

sources.title: Project Gigabit: UK subsidy advice
facts: The collection groups subsidy-control, wholesale-access, pricing and monitoring guidance.
Different guidance documents govern different stages of GIS intervention.
OMR and Public Review evidence does not itself impose open-access requirements.
Guidance update dates must be preserved.
Compliance guidance is not parcel availability evidence.

sources.title: Gigabit infrastructure subsidy guidance: wholesale access and pricing
facts: GIS-funded projects must incorporate wholesale pricing-control mechanisms.
Projects require benchmarking and price-control arrangements in supplier contracts.
The guidance applies to projects approved under the GIS scheme.
OMR and Public Review submissions are distinguished from contractual open-access duties.
Wholesale compliance does not prove retail service availability.

sources.title: BDUK Hubs Evaluation Plan
facts: The Hubs evaluation covers RGC Hubs and Project Gigabit GigaHubs.
The intervention funds gigabit connections to remote public buildings.
RGC operated from 2019 to 2022 and GigaHubs delivery spans 2022 to 2026.
The evaluation runs from 2022 to 2027.
Programme timelines do not establish current household connectivity.

sources.title: BDUK Project Gigabit Voucher Eligibility Engine transparency record
facts: The eligibility engine assesses whether a UK premise may qualify for a Project Gigabit voucher.
The transparency record identifies the system as a production planning capability.
The record documents organisational ownership and responsibility.
Eligibility logic is an administrative decision-support process.
An eligible classification is not evidence of delivered connectivity.
